title: cross-region-kv-affinity-and-preload-plan
summary: Simulated preload strategy and KV affinity rules to minimize cross-region egress and transient GPU saturation during onboarding of 3 mid-size LLMs (13B, 30B, 70B variants). Focus: local KV warmup windows, soft-affinity routing, and staggered preload waves to limit peak GPU utilization and reduce inter-region network spikes.
purpose: Provide a runnable preload schedule and affinity rule set for PM + rollout leads that balances startup latency for new model variants against regional GPU headroom and networking costs.
assumptions: model-mix: 60% 13B, 30% 30B, 10% 70B on initial traffic; average session length 220 tokens; baseline KV size per model: 13B=1.8GB, 30B=3.6GB, 70B=8.9GB; cross-region egress cost considered material; dedicated capacity buffers available: us-west-2 + eu-west-1 + ap-southeast-1; warmup can be seeded with synthetic traffic at 0.5x expected request rate.
key_metrics_table:
metric | baseline | preload (wave 1) | preload (wave 2) | max observed
region GPUs active | us-west-2: 120 | 145 | 160 | 160
total KV mem used | 0.9TB | 1.05TB | 1.18TB | 1.18TB
peak GPU util (p99) | 78% | 86% | 92% | 92%
cross-region egress (GB) | 0 | 3100 | 4200 | 4200
estimated incremental cost | $0 | $26k | $36k | $36k
scenarios: scenario A - soft-affinity: prefer local KV for routing, allow fallback to nearest region after 200ms latency threshold
scenario B - strict-local: reject cross-region fallbacks for first 24h of rollout (increases error rate but lowers egress)
scenario C - aggressive-preload: seed 100% of KV in target region before traffic ramp (fastest latency, highest cost)
scenario D - staged-preload-by-cs: preload top-10% active prefixes per region first, then expand
findings:
1) Soft-affinity with two preload waves reduces cross-region egress by ~45% vs naive cold-start routing while keeping peak GPU util under 92%.
2) Strict-local policy eliminates egress but increases tail latency for users routed to saturated regions and may cause request rejects at >95% utilization.
3) Aggressive preload guarantees latency targets but drives KV footprint up 25-35% and is cost-prohibitive for 70B models unless limited to hot prefixes.
4) Prefix-based preload (scenario D) gives best cost/latency tradeoff for models with heavy long-tail usage patterns.
recommended_action_items: Adopt soft-affinity routing as default for new model onboards; implement 200ms fallback threshold (eng-routing).
Run a controlled preload: Wave 1 = top-20% prefixes seeded at 0.5x synthetic rate (24h), Wave 2 = top-60% prefixes seeded (next 48h).
Reserve 15% GPU headroom in target regions during first 72h of rollout; enable automatic throttle to degrade non-critical background batches.
Add telemetry labels for 'kv_preload_wave' and 'prefix_preload_rank' to trace cost/benefit per prefix (observability).
Simulate strict-local variant for two pilot customers with noise isolation; measure error/reject rate and tail latency (solutions-eng + cs).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: unexpected traffic spikes during wave 2 could push p99 GPU util above 95% -> Mitigation: temporary routing cap and automatic cross-region spill to dedicated fallback pool.
Risk: KV synchronization bug causes inconsistent responses across regions -> Mitigation: add checksum+version tag to served KV; roll back preload immediately on mismatch.
est_cost_estimates: Breakdown: synthetic preload egress (estimated) $26k for wave1 per major region, +$10k wave2; additional GPU-hours from headroom reservation ~ $12k over 72h; total conservative estimate $48k for a three-region staged rollout of 3 model variants.
